clue.text: There's nothing loud in torch giving sudden illuminated burst

indicators.note: the word in tells us the two short pieces go inside the word for a torch

parts.note: a torch, in British English, is a battery-powered hand lamp, also called a flashlight
nothing is zero, written as the round letter O
F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud

explanation.surface: Someone asks why there is nothing loud about a torch that throws out a sudden beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'giving' are only link words. 'in' splits the torch word before LIGHT; in Britain a torch is a handheld battery lamp, not a flaming brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief flare or flicker of brightness is exactly a sudden illuminated burst, a phrase used for any momentary gleam.

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric

indicators.note: awful suggests the word tear is mangled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth has been badly ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' reads like a cut in fabric, but it is the definition; 'awful' makes RATE from the letters of tear.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash skin or cloth is to cut it deeply and raggedly, which is what lacerating means.

clue.text: In sargasso, dash of fizzy water

indicators.note: In tells us the letters sit inside the run of words sargasso, dash

explanation.surface: Someone adds a splash of sparkling water to a drink, perhaps in the Sargasso Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to the letters running across the end of sargasso and the start of dash. The Sargasso Sea is a region of the North Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is carbonated water, the bubbly mixer added to spirits.

definitions.meaning: abstaining from alcohol, an idiom from the water cart
literally riding on a cart while being transported

explanation.definitionFit: Being teetotal is an idiomatic sense of the phrase, and travelling in a horse-drawn cart is its literal sense.

definitions.meaning: to favour or incline towards something
a simple shed propped against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: To incline towards an option is one sense of the phrasal verb, and a lean-to is a small shed built against another building.

indicators.note: first says the piece from German comes at the front of the charade
half keeps only the opening three of the six letters of the word German

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial contraction meaning isn't

explanation.surface: A remark that a Welsh man is hardly German at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps GER, and 'first' puts it at the front. Geraint is a Welsh first name, borne by a knight of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraint is a traditionally Welsh given name, so a man bearing it is a typical Welshman in crossword terms.

clue.text: After six Greek character took mum into deity

indicators.note: After says the remaining pieces follow the Roman numeral for six

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
mum, as in keep mum, means silent, so the hushing word sh
nu is the Greek letter equivalent to N

explanation.surface: Following six, a Greek character took his mother along to meet a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' here means silence (keep mum), giving SH, not mother. Vishnu is a principal Hindu god.
explanation.definitionFit: Vishnu, the preserver, is one of the supreme gods of Hinduism, so a deity.

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
inc. is the usual short form of included

explanation.surface: The final character of something was included.
explanation.walkthrough: INC is the standard abbreviation of included, as on price lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a metallic chemical element, number 30 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Dorothy put mould next to printer

parts.note: Dot is a pet form of the name Dorothy
a matrix is a mould in which type or other objects are cast

explanation.surface: A woman called Dorothy set a mould beside the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... next to' just joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot-matrix machine prints characters as patterns of tiny inked dots from pins.

parts.note: creepy means eerie or mysterious in an unsettling way
crawly describes fawning, grovelling behaviour

explanation.surface: Someone mysterious and fawning is described as a tiny beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal term covers any small insect or spider, a little creature that scuttles.

parts.note: read as re-lease, meaning to let out again on a new contract, which is to take someone back on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Release' looks like setting free; split it as re-lease, to lease again, and the sense is to take on again.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease again is to hire again, an engagement renewed after an earlier one ended.

clue.text: Subatomic particle from Turin one gathered

indicators.note: gathered suggests the words Turin and one are pulled together and mixed up

explanation.surface: A tiny particle was collected in Turin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' shuffles the letters of TURIN and ONE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is an electrically neutral subatomic particle of almost no mass.

parts.note: a restaurant's service charge reimagined as a fee for a church service, which this kind of church would not levy

explanation.walkthrough: 'service charge' suggests a restaurant bill; the service is worship. A Free Church is a Protestant church outside the established Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonconformist church independent of the state church, jokingly read as one where worship costs nothing.

parts.note: the hot line is the imaginary circle round the middle of the Earth where it is hottest, not a telephone link

explanation.walkthrough: 'hot line' suggests an emergency phone link; it is the line of latitude at zero degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Places close to the Earth's middle latitude are described with this adjective, and they are typically hot.

indicators.note: unfolds suggests the word tale is opened out into a new order

explanation.surface: Elsewhere, too, a story is revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation can stand for et alibi, and elsewhere, as well as et alii, and others.

clue.text: Real sportsperson who is staunchly loyal

parts.note: true means real or genuine
a blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at a sport

explanation.surface: A genuine athlete who is steadfastly faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLUE is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsperson who has played against the other university, from the colours awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes unwavering faithfulness, especially to a political party such as the British Conservatives.

parts.note: ye is an old word for you
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to record a sudden shriek.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a short shrill cry, as of a dog in pain.

indicators.note: translation suggests the word braille is converted into a new form of letters

explanation.surface: A free rendering taken from braille.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean progressive and favouring reform, close to radical in political talk.

indicators.note: developed suggests the word comrade grows into a new arrangement

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A comrade without class developed a nervous jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' yields DEMOCRA from comrade's letters; 'Classless' looks like an insult but means egalitarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A society with equal rights for all, without privileged ranks, is egalitarian and so classless.

clue.text: Little bit brought up before first month for hard worker

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the month
brought up, in a down clue, means the word for a little bit is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ort is a scrap or small leftover of food
Jan is short for January, the first month

explanation.surface: A small item is raised ahead of January for a diligent employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' makes TRO in this down entry, and 'before' sets the month after it. To work like a Trojan is to work tirelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: From the phrase work like a Trojan, a Trojan is someone who labours with great energy.

clue.text: Straight round with expression of acquiescence

parts.note: right can mean straight, as in a right line
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A direct round accompanied by a word of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal exclamation signals agreement or assent, like saying okay.

parts.note: rubbish means nonsense, as in talking rubbish
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Valueless drivel from an unknown source.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of poor quality and little value is described as trashy or shoddy.

clue.text: Again from the beginning of French month at freezing-point

parts.note: de is French for of
Nov is short for November
water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, so O

explanation.surface: Starting afresh at the start of a frosty French month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' belongs to the definition, not an instruction to take a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means anew, starting over from scratch.

clue.text: Coal found by miner's leader under ocean

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, places the piece from miner's below the word for ocean

parts.note: sea is a word for ocean

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of miner's

explanation.surface: Coal discovered by a mining chief beneath the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' gives M, the first letter of miner's, and 'under' puts it after SEA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is a layer of coal in the ground that miners work, so the word can stand for the coal itself.

clue.text: What jockey must do to become drudge

definitions.meaning: a jockey's job is to ride and exert a racing mount
someone who does dull, heavy work

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a rider's duty to exert the mount, and as one word it means a tireless toiler.

clue.text: Airborne creature, one striking cowardly blows?

definitions.meaning: a flying thing, here a songbird of the bunting family
a striker who is yellow, meaning cowardly

explanation.definitionFit: The yellowhammer is a bright yellow bunting, and split in two the name describes a cowardly striking tool.
